diagnostic_evidence.quote: x^{k+1} = \mathop{\arg\min}_{x \in \cB(x^k, r)} \Big\{ \langle \nabla_x f(x^{k}, y^{k}), x \rangle + \frac{L_k}{2} \|x - x^k\|^2 + p(x) \Big\}.

$ p: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\} $ is proper closed convex, $ q:\mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\} $ is proper closed convex, and the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$ can be computed exactly.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 4 (equation (17)) of Algorithm 2 defines $x^{k+1}$ as the minimizer over the Euclidean ball constraint $\mathcal{B}(x^k, r)$. For a general proper closed convex function $p$, minimizing a quadratic plus $p$ over an intersecting Euclidean ball is not the standard proximal operator $\mathrm{prox}_{p/L_k}$, and cannot in general be evaluated by a single call to the proximal operator of $p$ (e.g., when $p(x) = \|x\|_1$, finding the Lagrange multiplier of the ball constraint requires solving a 1D root-finding problem involving multiple evaluations of the soft-thresholding operator). Assumption 1(ii) only assumes that the standard proximal operator of $p$ can be evaluated, so claiming that Algorithm 2 performs at most $\widehat{K}_\epsilon$ evaluations of the proximal operator of $p$ to solve problem (1) is unsupported and incorrect as stated.

failure_location.quote: We first observe from Algorithm 2 that the number of evaluations of the proximal operator $p$ equals the number of iterations. By this and $\overline{k} < \widehat{K}_\epsilon$, it follows that the total number of evaluations of $p$ to generate the $(\epsilon, \gamma \epsilon^\sigma / (4L_f))$-stationary point $x^{\overline{k}+1}$ is $\overline{k}+1 \leq \widehat{K}_\epsilon$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption 1(ii) to assume that the constrained proximal operator $\arg\min_{x \in \mathcal{B}(\bar{x}, r)} \{\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x - v\|^2 + p(x)\}$ can be computed exactly, or restrict $p$ to classes of functions (or indicator functions) where this subproblem can be solved in a single prox call, or account for the inner oracle complexity of solving the constrained subproblem (17).
issues.overall_effect: The complexity claim regarding the number of evaluations of the proximal operator of $p$ in Theorem 5 (and the corresponding prose summary in Remark 3 and the introduction) fails for general convex functions $p$.
issues.title: Subproblem in Algorithm 2 cannot be evaluated by a single proximal evaluation of p
issues.why_classification: The convergence analysis and iteration complexity of the outer method remain valid because $x^{k+1}$ is mathematically well-defined; the issue only concerns the oracle accounting for the proximal operator of $p$, which can be resolved either by strengthening the oracle assumption on $p$ or by a localized modification of the problem/assumption scope without altering the global proof architecture.
